title: Polynomial-time integer programming with bounded subdeterminants
formal: For every fixed \(\Delta\), is integer linear programming \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\in\mathbb Z^n\}\) polynomial-time solvable when all square subdeterminants of the integer matrix \(A\) have absolute value at most \(\Delta\)?

import_provenance.original_title: Polynomial-time integer programming with bounded subdeterminants
import_provenance.original_statement: For every fixed Δ, can arbitrary integer linear programs min{cᵀx:Ax≤b, x∈ℤⁿ} be solved in polynomial time when every square subdeterminant of the integer matrix A has absolute value at most Δ? Weismantel and coauthors’ bimodular algorithm handles Δ≤2; the question allows zero determinants and unrestricted row sparsity.
